name: banquish-mcp

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.description: Create a Workspace, named plainly after the task. By default use one per answer.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: List the user's Workspaces, most recently viewed first: id, name, Panel count, when the user last viewed it, and whether it is archived. With a query, only Workspaces whose name contains every word.

tools.name: rename_workspace
tools.description: Rename a Workspace, plainly. The user can undo it with the rest of your Working stretch.

tools.name: open_page
tools.description: Open a URL as a hidden Staging page with the user's profile: a page you may take Panels from, or one your own tools can't read properly. Find which pages to open with your own search; Banquish has no search. It waits for the page to settle (up to about 10 s), and you get the outline of its Candidate tree: the meaningful parts of the page, largest sections opened first, in at most 40 lines. The result holds the page id and the lines, each one string per candidate: `[id] ^parent kinds tag#htmlId.classes[role=…][aria="label"] @x,y wxh | counts | h:"heading" | "text" | +k`. ^parent is the candidate it sits in (^- for none); kinds are list:N (N items), item, ctl (a control), scrolls:H, fixed, or range a-b of n (a slice of a long level); @x,y wxh is its box on the page in CSS px; counts are the images, media, buttons, inputs and links inside it, left out when none; h: is its heading and "text" the start of its text; +k counts candidates inside it not shown. The result says if the page still shows a loading screen, and names the HTTP status when the page answered with an error (400 or above). Use expand and find to see more, as the page is then; ids stay valid while their candidates are on the page. Only your few most recently used pages keep running: one you leave behind (or unused for a few minutes) is unloaded to save memory and opened again when you next use it, keeping the ids of what's still in the same place. Pages on the user's Private sites are refused.

tools.name: expand
tools.description: Show a candidate's children on an open page as it is now, in at most 40 lines like open_page's, opening the largest first. A candidate with more than 40 children is paged: pass pageNo for the next pages. Says how many candidates the page gained since you last looked (+N new), with new ids. If the page can't be read again, it is closed: open it again with open_page.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Find the smallest candidates on an open page, as it is now, whose text, heading, label, id or classes contain every word, in at most 40 lines like open_page's. Says how many candidates the page gained since you last looked (+N new). If the page can't be read again, it is closed: open it again with open_page.

tools.name: reveal
tools.description: Reveal content hidden behind a control on an open page (a tab, an expand toggle, a disclosure, a "more" button): Banquish clicks the candidate for you (or the one button or link inside it, when it holds just one), stopping any request that could write, any navigation and any new window meanwhile, and checks that new content appeared. Returns the updated tree in lines like open_page's: the new candidates, then the outline. Ids you had stay valid; new content gets new ids. A Panel made from the page afterwards comes back in the revealed view after a reload. If the click tries to navigate or open a window, moves the page to another path, or shows nothing new, the reveal is refused with the reason: use content reachable by URL instead. Never on the user's Private sites. Reveals on different pages may run in parallel.

tools.name: add_panel
tools.description: Propose a Panel from candidate ids of an open page. Banquish confirms it on the page, which the first Panel from it takes over as its own. The page stays open to you for more Panels: its ids stay valid for expand, find, add_panel and update_panel, and each further Panel gets a fresh copy of the page, where Banquish replays your reveals and finds the parts again, which takes a few seconds (refused if they aren't found). reveal and screenshot need the page opened again once a Panel has taken it. Each id is one part; several ids make one Composite Panel, for parts of the page that act on each other (a player and its transcript, a chart and its time picker): they show together in one tile and stay live together. exclude takes ids of candidates inside the chosen parts that the Panel leaves out (an ad, a reply box, the rest of a container whose text you want); any other id is refused with the reason. Mode is "item" (follow this specific thing, the default) or "spot" (whatever occupies this place). Placement is where its Tile goes on the Workspace's grid, as in arrange; without one it goes full width below the last Tile. With h, a Panel's Tile is that tall where its Panel is taller, and its Panel scrolls inside it; h beyond its Panel's own height is capped at that height, and the Fit report says so (capped). Returns the Fit report: at the user's window, which Tiles are scaled below their Panel's minimum width, have an h taller than their Panel (capped, with the h they got), scroll inside, fell back to crop, are broken or ambiguous, or leave their Tile's width unused, and any gaps between Tiles. A Tile whose page hasn't laid it out at its width yet (one not on screen, say) is settling: a later report says how it fits. While a settling Tile's minimum width isn't known, whether the Workspace shows as one column isn't either: oneColumn is left out, and the summary says so.

tools.name: read_workspace
tools.description: Read a Workspace: every Tile in one list, in reading order (top to bottom, then left to right), and the user's current window size. Each Tile has its kind and placement on the grid: x and w in 12 columns, y and h in rows of 8 px at the user's laptop window (1512 px wide; gaps 16 px, margins 24 px), each y being where the Tile floats up to. No h means the Tile is as tall as its Panel or Note, at most about two-thirds of the user's window height (a taller Panel scrolls inside it). With h, a Panel's Tile is that tall where its Panel is taller, and its Panel scrolls inside it; h beyond its Panel's own height is capped at that height, and the Fit report says so (capped). With h, a Note's Tile is that tall, even taller than its text. A Panel has its id, Source page, mode, state (live while it shows its content; restoring, paused, broken, ambiguous, needs-peek or not-responding otherwise) and Fit status at the user's window, as the Fit report gives it. tier says how its content was last found: exact, healed (found by similarity after a reload), ambiguous (with the candidate ids on its running page that might be it) or not-found; moved means an item-mode Panel found its content somewhere else on the page. A Note has its id, text and when it was last written. A hidden Tile is a Panel from one of the user's Private sites: only its placement, which you can't move or remove. On a Panel or Note, userChanged means the user moved or resized it since you last placed Tiles on this Workspace (with arrange, or add_panel or add_note with a placement).

tools.name: arrange
tools.description: Place any number of Tiles (Panels and Notes, by id) on a Workspace's grid in one call: x and w in 12 columns, y and h in rows of 8 px at the user's laptop window (1512 px wide; gaps 16 px, margins 24 px). No h means the Tile is as tall as its Panel or Note, at most about two-thirds of the user's window height (a taller Panel scrolls inside it). With h, a Panel's Tile is that tall where its Panel is taller, and its Panel scrolls inside it; h beyond its Panel's own height is capped at that height, and the Fit report says so (capped). With h, a Note's Tile is that tall, even taller than its text. Only the listed Tiles move. Tiles float up: y orders them, and each sits right under whatever is above it in its columns; a Tile placed on others pushes them, and those under them, down, hidden Tiles too. x + w over 12, or a negative or zero value, is refused with the reason, and then nothing moves; so is a Tile you can't see. A width below a Panel's minimum is taken, and the Panel shows scaled. Returns every Tile's placement. Returns the Fit report: at the user's window, which Tiles are scaled below their Panel's minimum width, have an h taller than their Panel (capped, with the h they got), scroll inside, fell back to crop, are broken or ambiguous, or leave their Tile's width unused, and any gaps between Tiles. A Tile whose page hasn't laid it out at its width yet (one not on screen, say) is settling: a later report says how it fits. While a settling Tile's minimum width isn't known, whether the Workspace shows as one column isn't either: oneColumn is left out, and the summary says so.

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Add a Note to a Workspace: a few words of your own beside its Panels. Formatted text only, shown in Banquish's own style: "# Heading" (or "## Smaller heading"), paragraphs, "- " or "1. " list items, and [links](https://…); anything else, HTML included, shows as the text it is. At most 2000 characters. Placement is where its Tile goes on the grid, as in arrange; without one it goes full width below the last Tile. With h, a Note's Tile is that tall, even taller than its text. The user can undo it with the rest of your Working stretch. Returns the Fit report: at the user's window, which Tiles are scaled below their Panel's minimum width, have an h taller than their Panel (capped, with the h they got), scroll inside, fell back to crop, are broken or ambiguous, or leave their Tile's width unused, and any gaps between Tiles. A Tile whose page hasn't laid it out at its width yet (one not on screen, say) is settling: a later report says how it fits. While a settling Tile's minimum width isn't known, whether the Workspace shows as one column isn't either: oneColumn is left out, and the summary says so.

tools.name: update_note
tools.description: Rewrite a Note's text, in the same formatted text as add_note. It keeps its id and placement; place it with arrange. The user can undo it with the rest of your Working stretch. Returns the Fit report: at the user's window, which Tiles are scaled below their Panel's minimum width, have an h taller than their Panel (capped, with the h they got), scroll inside, fell back to crop, are broken or ambiguous, or leave their Tile's width unused, and any gaps between Tiles. A Tile whose page hasn't laid it out at its width yet (one not on screen, say) is settling: a later report says how it fits. While a settling Tile's minimum width isn't known, whether the Workspace shows as one column isn't either: oneColumn is left out, and the summary says so.

tools.name: remove_note
tools.description: Remove a Note from its Workspace. The user can undo it with the rest of your Working stretch. Returns the Fit report: at the user's window, which Tiles are scaled below their Panel's minimum width, have an h taller than their Panel (capped, with the h they got), scroll inside, fell back to crop, are broken or ambiguous, or leave their Tile's width unused, and any gaps between Tiles. A Tile whose page hasn't laid it out at its width yet (one not on screen, say) is settling: a later report says how it fits. While a settling Tile's minimum width isn't known, whether the Workspace shows as one column isn't either: oneColumn is left out, and the summary says so.

tools.name: update_panel
tools.description: Change a Panel: re-propose its content, change what it leaves out, or switch it between Item and Spot mode, in any combination. Re-proposing is how you resolve an ambiguous or broken Panel when the user asks you to. For an ambiguous Panel, give candidates from the ids read_workspace offers for it. Otherwise open its Source page (or another) with open_page and give that page with candidate ids from it. The page is used as add_panel uses it: the first Panel from it takes it over as its own, and it stays open to you for more Panels; from a page a Panel has taken, the Panel gets a fresh copy where Banquish replays your reveals and finds the parts again (refused if they aren't found, and the Panel gets its old content back). Several ids make a Composite Panel. exclude takes ids of candidates inside the chosen parts that the Panel leaves out. Given without candidates, exclude changes what the Panel leaves out of its parts, with ids from the page you made it from while that page is still open to you; [] brings everything back. mode is "item" (follow this specific thing) or "spot" (whatever occupies this place): from then on the Panel finds its content that way: at once, and again whenever its page loads. The Panel keeps its id and placement; place it with arrange.

tools.name: remove_panel
tools.description: Remove a Panel from its Workspace (a hidden Tile can't be removed). The user can undo it with the rest of your Working stretch. Returns the Fit report: at the user's window, which Tiles are scaled below their Panel's minimum width, have an h taller than their Panel (capped, with the h they got), scroll inside, fell back to crop, are broken or ambiguous, or leave their Tile's width unused, and any gaps between Tiles. A Tile whose page hasn't laid it out at its width yet (one not on screen, say) is settling: a later report says how it fits. While a settling Tile's minimum width isn't known, whether the Workspace shows as one column isn't either: oneColumn is left out, and the summary says so.

tools.name: read_panel
tools.description: Read a Panel's current identity and values, kept apart (identity: what it is, e.g. heading, label, link; values: prices, counts, times), with its state and how fresh the read is. Banquish reloads an unloaded page if needed. To protect sites, values read under a minute ago are served as they are, and an unloaded page is reloaded at most every 5 minutes: reads in between get the last values, stale since they were read. A not-responding Panel's page isn't reloaded for a read: it waits for the user to reload it.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: An image of one candidate of an open page, and nothing else, for content text can't describe (a canvas chart, an image). Use it sparingly: the Candidate tree usually says enough.

tools.name: workspace_image
tools.description: A JPEG of a Workspace as the user's window shows it now (the part in view). With width (CSS pixels), a preview of the whole Workspace at that window width instead: the placement adapted to that width, each Tile's last frame rescaled, so it's approximate. A Workspace not on the user's screen is previewed at the user's window width. Tiles you can't see (Private sites') are plain boxes labelled "Private site".

tools.name: finish_work
tools.description: Signal that you've finished working: the working mark clears, Staging pages no Panel came from are discarded, your changes become one step the user can undo, and the user is told your answer is ready on the Workspaces you changed. No Fit report is sent after it.

instructions:
Banquish lets you answer with the live web: you compose live parts of real pages (Panels) and short Notes on a Workspace the user sees. Open a page with open_page, find the parts with expand and find (reveal what a tab or toggle hides), add them with add_panel, place Tiles with arrange, label them with add_note, and call finish_work when you are done.

Finding pages:
- Find which sites and items to consider with your own search: Banquish has no search.
- Open in Banquish the pages you may take Panels from, and any page your own tools can't read properly: blocked, rendered by scripts, visual (a map, a chart), signed in, or depending on the user's own view (their size, region or prices).
- Never take current values (prices, rates, scores) from search summaries: they go stale, and the Panels carry them.
- When the user says "use Banquish", they mean answer in Banquish, not skip searching.

Composing a Workspace:
- Compose for the user's window: read_workspace and every Fit report say its size. Banquish adapts your composition to other windows (zoomed on wider ones, re-flowed on narrower ones, one column when too narrow), so don't compose for other sizes.
- Keep the Tiles the user changed (userChanged in read_workspace, and "Since your last call") as they are, unless the task needs otherwise.
- Hidden Tiles are the user's Panels from Private sites: they take space you compose around, and you can't move or remove them.
- Notes say what the pieces are or why they are there: a heading over a group, a label that tells peers apart. Never quote values in a Note (prices, counts, times): they go stale while the Panels stay live.
- For "the top N" of a ranked list, add its rows in Spot mode, so the Panel shows whatever holds those places as the ranking changes; Item mode follows those specific rows.
- Check the result with the Fit report that every placing call returns, and with workspace_image when it is unclear.

Banquish isn't set up on this computer: /tmp/.banquish/bin/banquish is missing.

banquish-mcp runs the MCP server of Banquish, a Mac app (Apple silicon) that composes live parts of real pages into a Workspace you see.

1. Install Banquish: download it from https://banquish.space, or run
     brew install --cask banquish-app/tap/banquish
2. Open Banquish once. That installs /tmp/.banquish/bin/banquish.
3. Restart your MCP client.
